{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reviews rodent models of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and compares treatment efficacy from preclinical testing with outcomes from clinical trials, explicitly stating it investigates 'the translatability of preclinical disease models by comparing the treatment efficacy in rodent models of DKD with corresponding results from clinical studies.' This directly addresses the concordance between animal model results and human clinical outcomes for treatment efficacy.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "In this review, we investigate the translatability of preclinical disease models by comparing the treatment efficacy in rodent models of DKD with corresponding results from clinical studies.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "renal",
    "metabolic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD).",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "Many rodent models are available for investigating the pathophysiology of DKD and testing of novel therapeutic strategies (Table 1).",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Rodent models of diabetic kidney disease Many rodent models are available for investigating the pathophysiology of DKD and testing of novel therapeutic strategies (Table 1).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The main renal outcomes of a subset of these clinical trials are summarized in Table 3, with comparison to corresponding data from preclinical studies in rodent models of DKD. Included is the spectrum from smaller exploratory trials, often with albuminuria outcomes, to large cardiovascular outcomes trials (CVOTs) wherein antidiabetic agents were tested for non-inferiority (and for the SGLT2i and GLP1 analog-classes of drugs, showed superiority and clinically very relevant CV benefits), and the more recent renal outcome trials initiated following promising results in the CVOTs. The latter used CKD outcomes as primary endpoints including eGFR, progression of albuminuria, doubling of serum creatinine, incidence of ESRD (or need for renal replacement therapy), and death from renal causes."
}
